identity: WUR BIN / 56837 /1001O6087; Dutch-taught, full-time three-year BSc

components.reviewedClaim: Communication theories applied to global crises, media, framing, information and unequal policy responses.
Historical/geographical development processes, inequality, colonialism and institutions; critical literature and writing.
First-year skills trajectories, career reflection and personal study roadmap.
Economic models and evidence explain real-world inequality, sustainability and economic change.
Foundational sociology and its application to development and communication; cannot combine with HSO11305, which is absent.
Anthropology of law: unequal power, land tenure, property, NGOs, human rights and development change.
Research questions and feasible proposal design using experiments, cross-sectional study and case studies.
Technology and natural resources mediated by social-group interactions; Ghana, South Africa and India cases.
Probability, descriptive statistics, testing and estimation; statistical ethics.
Means, confidence intervals, regression, correlation and model assumptions; Statistics 1 provides preparation.
Critical sociological perspectives on agriculture and rural change in Global North/South, beyond modernisation logic.
Multidisciplinary group analysis of a societal problem through proposal, literature/interviews and written/oral reporting.
Development theories, poverty/distribution, agricultural transformation, institutions, markets, trade and globalisation.
Gender/diversity, unequal histories and ethics of care frame reflection on sustainability responsibilities.
Global public/private/civil institutions, legitimacy, effectiveness and sustainable-development governance.
Historical globalisation, international order, power and uneven economic/technological change.
Contextual history of development/growth ideas, including non-Western and degrowth perspectives.
Major contemporary sociologists applied to sustainability, inequality and humanitarian/climate questions.
Complementary economic and sociological/anthropological analysis of rural-household livelihood strategies and policy.
Environmental externalities, policy instruments, effectiveness and efficiency; introductory economics and basic calculus are advisory preparation.
Qualitative and quantitative field-research proposal, sampling, observation, interviews, questionnaires, SPSS, reflexivity and ethics.
Two weeks individual field research in NL/England/Ireland, preceded by proposal and followed by analysis/report; safety required, SDC21306/DEC20306 advise preparation.
Social structures, institutions, agency, state and class/gender/race power in development; sociological theory prepares study.
Food networks, production/consumption, global flows, consumer concerns, regulation, certification and alternative supply chains.
Agrarian change, labour, farming diversity, access/property, social reproduction, technologies and movements; field safety mandatory.
Sociological/anthropological planetary development debates: power, exclusion, activism, conservation, rural/urban futures and migration.

12-credit supervised literature review with optional empirical supplement, research questions/planning and written report. At least two of ENP31806, RSO21306, RSO30806, SDC30306 mandatory; this pathway includes all four.

openSpace.status: minor and/or individual elective courses; no compulsory package

routeSelection.basis: The generic target has three equally formal 36-EC specialisations: Sociology of Development, Economics of Development, and Politics and Communication in Development. None is identified as the general route, so the first current handbook specialisation is selected neutrally and independently of UCR fit.

entryAndProgression: Three equally formal 36-credit specialisations; selected A Sociology of Development by current official-order tie-break, independently of UCR fit.
114 common +24 taught specialisation +12 thesis +30 open =180 unique credits. No other route modules counted.

General Safety ZSS06000 and Fieldwork Safety ZSS06200 are zero-credit obligations, not invented EC. Complete safety before relevant field activities; RSO30806 and SDC21306/22306 explicitly require fieldwork safety.

Thesis group requires 102 compulsory/restricted credits including all60 first-year credits and mandatory thesis knowledge. This pathway completes all138 prescribed taught credits, allB1 and allfour named specialisation courses before YSS82812; exceeds minimumtwo of four.

YSS82812 refers to programme study guide as assumed knowledge, while current programme and module explicitly supply credit/mandatory-course gates and supervisor consultation; no unsupported additional formal gate inferred.

Advisory economics/statistics/sociology/research sequences checked. Choose entrant with VWO Mathematics B preparation (admitted on current Dutch overview), supporting basic calculus for ENR20306 without adding credits. First-year research/problem-analysis and rural-livelihoods courses prepare second-year field methods/practical.
Fieldwork locations verified from current overview and SDC22306; no compulsory Global South placement claimed. Thesis empirical research is optional, not mandatory.
controllingEvidence: Current 2026 study-handbook programme groups and module records control codes, credits and entry; Dutch overview corroborates pedagogy, formal routes, elective space and outcomes. English overview is concise and does not independently substantiate all old interest claims.
